# LangSmith CLI reference for coding agents

<!-- Generated by `langsmith docs agents` from the command tree and internal/cmd/agent_reference.yaml. Do not edit; run `make agent-docs`. -->

How to use the `langsmith` CLI from a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others) to read and manage LangSmith data. Sections are organized by task; the [All commands](#all-commands) table at the end lists everything this version supports. Every command and flag below exists in this version of the CLI, and `langsmith <command> --help` shows the rest.

Rules of thumb:

- Pass `--format json` (or `--jq`) on every call and parse the JSON. The default `pretty` output is for humans and may change.
- Start narrow: set `--limit` and a time window (`--last-n-minutes` or `--since`), then widen.
- Never run a delete without the user's explicit approval. See [Safety](#safety).

## Basics

### Global flags

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--api-url string` | LangSmith API URL [env: LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT] |
| `--format string` | Output format: pretty or json |
| `--profile string` | Named profile to use [env: LANGSMITH_PROFILE] |
| `--workspace string` | LangSmith workspace ID [env: LANGSMITH_WORKSPACE_ID] |

### Authentication

Set `LANGSMITH_API_KEY` in the environment; it is the most reliable option for agents and CI because it needs no browser or saved state. `langsmith auth login` opens a browser for OAuth and suits people, not agents. Check what the CLI will use with `langsmith auth info --format json`.

For a self-hosted or regional instance, also set `LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT` (or pass `--api-url`). If the key can reach more than one workspace, set `LANGSMITH_WORKSPACE_ID` (or pass `--workspace`). Set `LANGSMITH_PROJECT` to give trace and run commands a default project.

Don't print API keys, and don't put them on the command line where they end up in shell history.

### Output

- `--format json` prints machine-readable JSON. Lists print a JSON array.
- `--jq EXPR` filters the JSON output with a jq expression and implies `--format json`, e.g. `--jq '.[].id'`. No separate `jq` install is needed.
- Many read commands take `-o FILE` (`--output`) to write the JSON to a file instead of stdout, which keeps large payloads out of the agent's context.
- Trace and run commands return compact rows by default. Add `--include-io` for inputs, outputs and errors, `--include-metadata` for status, latency, tokens and costs, `--include-feedback` for feedback scores, or `--full` for all three.
- Errors go to stderr and the exit code is non-zero.

### Paging and time windows

List commands return a bounded page; set the size with `--limit` (`-n`). Trace and run queries cover the last 7 days unless you pass `--since`, `--before` or `--last-n-minutes`. To read further back, page with `--before` set to the oldest `start_time` you have seen.

These commands page with `--cursor`: `langsmith hub list`, `langsmith prompt commits`, `langsmith prompt list`, `langsmith runs list`, `langsmith threads messages`, `langsmith traces list`, `langsmith traces messages`. Passing `--cursor ""` on the first call adds `cursors.next` to the JSON output (list commands then wrap their items in an object); pass that value to `--cursor` to get the next page. A missing `cursors.next` means there are no more results.

### Safety

Get the user's explicit approval before running any delete. Some deletes run immediately with no prompt.

Deletes marked *confirms* in [All commands](#all-commands) print a warning to stderr and wait for `y` on stdin; without an answer they abort. Do not answer the prompt or pipe `y` into it: stop and ask the user. Only after the user approves that specific deletion, rerun the command with `--yes`.

Commands that create or update resources (datasets, examples, prompts, evaluator rules, annotation queues) change shared workspace data. Confirm the target with a `get` or `list` first, and prefer IDs over names when you build a command line.

## Find traces and runs

A trace is one top-level agent invocation and its tree of runs; a run is one step (LLM call, tool call, chain). Find the project first, then query traces or runs in it. Pass `--project-id` rather than `--project` when you have the UUID.

### `langsmith projects list`

List tracing projects in the workspace (default: 20, sorted by most recent activity)

Usage: `langsmith projects list [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--name-contains string` | Filter projects by name substring |
| `-n, --limit int` | Maximum number of projects to return |

```bash
langsmith projects list --name-contains my-app --format json
```

### `langsmith traces list`

List traces (root runs) matching filter criteria (default: 20, newest first)

Usage: `langsmith traces list [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--project string` | Project name [env: LANGSMITH_PROJECT] |
| `--project-id string` | Project (session) UUID; skips the name lookup. Mutually exclusive with --project; overrides $LANGSMITH_PROJECT |
| `-n, --limit int` | Maximum number of results to return |
| `--last-n-minutes int` | Only include runs from the last N minutes, e.g. 60 (overrides 7-day default) |
| `--since string` | Only include runs after this timestamp, e.g. 2024-01-15T00:00:00Z (overrides 7-day default) |
| `--before string` | Only include runs before this timestamp, e.g. 2024-01-15T00:00:00Z (for pagination) |
| `--error` | Filter for failed runs only |
| `--filter string` | LangSmith filter DSL, e.g. 'and(eq(run_type, "llm"), gte(latency, 5))'. Match metadata with 'and(eq(metadata_key, "user_id"), eq(metadata_value, "u1"))', and inputs or outputs with input_key/input_value or output_key/output_value; metadata.x and inputs.x paths are not supported |
| `--metadata string` | Filter by metadata key=value (e.g. revision_id=abc123) |
| `--tags string` | Comma-separated tags (OR logic) |
| `--full` | Shorthand for --include-metadata --include-io --include-feedback |
| `--show-hierarchy` | Fetch the full run tree for each trace |

```bash
langsmith traces list --project my-app --last-n-minutes 60 --limit 10 --format json
langsmith traces list --project my-app --metadata user_id=u_123 --include-metadata --format json
```

### `langsmith runs list`

List runs matching filter criteria (default: 50, newest first)

Usage: `langsmith runs list [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--project string` | Project name [env: LANGSMITH_PROJECT] |
| `--run-type string` | Filter by run type (llm, chain, tool, retriever, prompt, parser) |
| `--name string` | Filter by run name (exact match) |
| `-n, --limit int` | Maximum number of results to return |
| `--last-n-minutes int` | Only include runs from the last N minutes, e.g. 60 (overrides 7-day default) |
| `--error` | Filter for failed runs only |
| `--min-latency float64` | Minimum latency in seconds |
| `--min-tokens int` | Minimum total tokens |
| `--filter string` | LangSmith filter DSL, e.g. 'and(eq(run_type, "llm"), gte(latency, 5))'. Match metadata with 'and(eq(metadata_key, "user_id"), eq(metadata_value, "u1"))', and inputs or outputs with input_key/input_value or output_key/output_value; metadata.x and inputs.x paths are not supported |
| `--trace-ids string` | Comma-separated trace IDs to filter by |
| `--full` | Shorthand for --include-metadata --include-io --include-feedback |

```bash
langsmith runs list --project my-app --run-type llm --min-latency 5 --limit 20 --format json
langsmith runs list --project my-app --run-type tool --error --include-io --format json
```

### `langsmith threads list`

List conversation threads in a project (default: 20, newest first)

Usage: `langsmith threads list [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--project string` | Project name [env: LANGSMITH_PROJECT] |
| `-n, --limit int` | Maximum number of threads to return |
| `--last-n-minutes int` | Only include threads active in last N minutes |
| `--filter string` | LangSmith filter DSL, e.g. 'and(eq(run_type, "llm"), gte(latency, 5))'. Match metadata with 'and(eq(metadata_key, "user_id"), eq(metadata_value, "u1"))', and inputs or outputs with input_key/input_value or output_key/output_value; metadata.x and inputs.x paths are not supported |

Threads group traces that share a thread ID (a multi-turn conversation).

```bash
langsmith threads list --project my-app --limit 10 --format json
```

### `langsmith traces stats`

Aggregate stats for traces in a project (token usage, latency, costs, feedback)

Usage: `langsmith traces stats [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--project string` | Project name [env: LANGSMITH_PROJECT] |
| `--since string` | Start of time window (RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD; default: 7 days ago) |
| `--last-n-minutes int` | Shorthand: window = last N minutes (overrides --since) |
| `--filter string` | LangSmith filter DSL (applied to both windows if comparing) |
| `--compare-last-n-minutes int` | Shorthand: comparison window = N minutes before the primary window starts |

Use stats for "how many / how slow / how expensive" questions instead of listing every trace.

```bash
langsmith traces stats --project my-app --last-n-minutes 1440 --compare-last-n-minutes 1440 --format json
```

## Debug a failure

List failed traces, open one with its inputs, outputs and errors, then drill into the failing run. For a conversation, read the thread's messages.

### `langsmith traces get`

Fetch every run in a single trace

Usage: `langsmith traces get TRACE_ID [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--project string` | Project name [env: LANGSMITH_PROJECT] |
| `--full` | Shorthand for --include-metadata --include-io --include-feedback |
| `--include-io` | Add inputs, outputs, error, and events fields |
| `-o, --output string` | Write JSON output to a file |

Prints every run in the trace. Use `-o` for large traces and read the file.

```bash
langsmith traces list --project my-app --error --last-n-minutes 60 --format json --jq '.[].trace_id'
langsmith traces get 0190a3c4-1234-7abc-8def-0123456789ab --project my-app --full -o trace.json
```

### `langsmith runs get`

Fetch a single run by its run ID

Usage: `langsmith runs get RUN_ID [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--full` | Shorthand for --include-metadata --include-io --include-feedback |
| `--include-io` | Add inputs, outputs, error, and events fields |
| `-o, --output string` | Write JSON output to a file |

```bash
langsmith runs get 0190a3c4-1234-7abc-8def-0123456789ab --full --format json
```

### `langsmith threads messages`

Get conversation messages for a thread

Usage: `langsmith threads messages THREAD_ID [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--project string` | Project name [env: LANGSMITH_PROJECT] |
| `-n, --limit int` | Maximum number of turns to return (max 100) |
| `--cursor string` | Pagination cursor from a previous response |

```bash
langsmith threads messages my-thread-id --project my-app --format json
```

### `langsmith traces export`

Export traces to a directory as JSONL files (one file per trace)

Usage: `langsmith traces export OUTPUT_DIR [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--project string` | Project name [env: LANGSMITH_PROJECT] |
| `-n, --limit int` | Maximum number of results to return |
| `--error` | Filter for failed runs only |
| `--full` | Shorthand for --include-metadata --include-io --include-feedback |
| `--filename-pattern string` | Filename pattern. Supports {trace_id} and {name} placeholders. |

Writes one JSONL file per trace, for offline analysis of many traces.

```bash
langsmith traces export ./failed-traces --project my-app --error --limit 50 --full
```

## Datasets and examples

Datasets hold examples (inputs and reference outputs) for offline evaluation. Most dataset commands take a name or a UUID.

### `langsmith datasets list`

List all datasets in the workspace (default: 100)

Usage: `langsmith datasets list [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--name-contains string` | Filter datasets by name substring |
| `-n, --limit int` | Maximum number of datasets to return |

```bash
langsmith datasets list --name-contains qa --format json
```

### `langsmith datasets get`

Get dataset details by name or UUID

Usage: `langsmith datasets get NAME_OR_ID [flags]`

```bash
langsmith datasets get my-dataset --format json
```

### `langsmith datasets create`

Create a new empty dataset

Usage: `langsmith datasets create [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--name string` | Name for the new dataset (required) |
| `--description string` | Optional description |

```bash
langsmith datasets create --name my-dataset --description "Support questions" --format json
```

### `langsmith datasets upload`

Upload a JSON file as a new dataset

Usage: `langsmith datasets upload FILE_PATH [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--name string` | Name for the new dataset (required) |
| `--description string` | Optional description |

```bash
langsmith datasets upload examples.json --name my-dataset --format json
```

### `langsmith datasets export`

Export dataset examples to a JSON file

Usage: `langsmith datasets export NAME_OR_ID OUTPUT_FILE [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `-n, --limit int` | Maximum number of examples to export |

```bash
langsmith datasets export my-dataset examples.json --limit 1000
```

### `langsmith examples list`

List examples in a dataset (default: 20)

Usage: `langsmith examples list [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--dataset string` | Dataset name or UUID (required) |
| `--split string` | Filter by split (train, test, validation) |
| `-n, --limit int` | Maximum number of examples to return |
| `--offset int` | Number of examples to skip (pagination) |

```bash
langsmith examples list --dataset my-dataset --limit 50 --format json
```

### `langsmith examples create`

Create a new example in a dataset

Usage: `langsmith examples create [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--dataset string` | Dataset name (required) |
| `--inputs string` | JSON string of input fields (required) |
| `--outputs string` | JSON string of output fields |
| `--metadata string` | JSON string of metadata |
| `--split string` | Assign to a split (train, test, validation) |

```bash
langsmith examples create --dataset my-dataset --inputs '{"question":"What is LangSmith?"}' --outputs '{"answer":"An observability and evaluation platform"}'
```

### `langsmith examples update`

Update a specific example.

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--example-id string` | — |
| `--inputs string=any` | New inputs. Replaces the existing inputs; omit to keep them. |
| `--outputs string=any` | New outputs. Replaces the existing outputs; omit to keep them. |
| `--metadata string=any` | New metadata. Replaces the existing metadata; omit to keep it. |
| `--split` | Split or splits to put the example in. Replaces its current splits. |

Each of `--inputs`, `--outputs` and `--metadata` replaces the whole field; omit a flag to keep its current value.

## Experiments

An experiment is one evaluation run over a dataset. List the experiments on a dataset, then read one for its per-example results and feedback scores.

### `langsmith experiments list`

List experiments, optionally filtered by dataset (default: 20)

Usage: `langsmith experiments list [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--dataset string` | Filter to experiments for this dataset |
| `-n, --limit int` | Maximum number of experiments to return |

```bash
langsmith experiments list --dataset my-dataset --format json
```

### `langsmith experiments get`

Get detailed results for a specific experiment

Usage: `langsmith experiments get NAME_OR_ID [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `-o, --output string` | Write JSON output to a file |

```bash
langsmith experiments get my-experiment -o experiment.json
```

## Prompts

Prompts live in Prompt Hub repos named `OWNER/REPO`. Each push creates a commit; tags point at commits.

### `langsmith prompt list`

List Prompt Hub repos

Usage: `langsmith prompt list [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--query string` | Filter by name/description substring |
| `-n, --limit int` | Maximum number of prompts to return |
| `--cursor string` | Resume after the last item of a previous call by passing its cursors.next. Passing --cursor (even "" for the first page) adds cursors.next to the JSON output |

```bash
langsmith prompt list --query support --format json
```

### `langsmith prompt pull`

Fetch a prompt's manifest (latest or a specific commit/tag)

Usage: `langsmith prompt pull OWNER/REPO[:COMMIT_OR_TAG] [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--commit string` | Commit hash or tag name (overrides inline :ref) |
| `-o, --output string` | Write JSON output to a file |

```bash
langsmith prompt pull my-org/support-agent:production --format json
```

### `langsmith prompt push`

Push a new commit (manifest) to a Prompt Hub repo

Usage: `langsmith prompt push OWNER/REPO [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `-f, --file string` | Path to manifest JSON file (reads stdin if omitted) |
| `--description string` | Commit description / message (optional) |

```bash
langsmith prompt push my-org/support-agent --file manifest.json --description "Tighten refusal wording"
```

### `langsmith prompt create`

Create a new Prompt Hub repo

Usage: `langsmith prompt create [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--name string` | Repo handle / slug (required) |
| `--description string` | Optional description |
| `--public` | Make the repo public |
| `--tags stringSlice` | Tags for the repo (comma-separated) |

### `langsmith prompt tag update`

Move a tag to a different commit

Usage: `langsmith prompt tag update OWNER/REPO TAG_NAME [flags]`

## Evaluators and rules

An evaluator scores runs. A rule attaches an evaluator to a tracing project (online evaluation) or a dataset (offline evaluation), with a sampling rate and filter.

### `langsmith evaluators list`

List evaluators and the projects or datasets each one is attached to

Usage: `langsmith evaluators list [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--name-contains string` | Filter by name substring |
| `--type string` | Filter by evaluator type (llm or code) |

```bash
langsmith evaluators list --type llm --format json
```

### `langsmith evaluators get`

Get an evaluator by name or ID

Usage: `langsmith evaluators get NAME_OR_ID [flags]`

```bash
langsmith evaluators get correctness --format json
```

### `langsmith evaluators create-llm`

Create an LLM-as-judge evaluator rule

Usage: `langsmith evaluators create-llm [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--name string` | Evaluator name (required); --replace matches an existing rule on the target by rule or evaluator name |
| `--project string` | Target project name |
| `--dataset string` | Target dataset name |
| `--prompt string` | Prompt JSON file ([[role,content],...] or [{role,content},...]); omit if --hub-ref is set |
| `--hub-ref string` | Prompt Hub reference; replaces --prompt and --schema (e.g. my-org/prompt:latest) |
| `--model-config string` | Serialized LangChain model JSON (required; copy from UI or GET /runs/rules) |
| `--schema string` | JSON schema file for structured output; omit if --hub-ref is set |
| `--variable-mapping string` | Map prompt vars to trace paths (JSON or @file.json) |
| `--sampling-rate float64` | Fraction of runs to evaluate (0.0-1.0); --replace keeps the rule's current rate unless this is set |
| `--trace-filter string` | Filter expression for which runs to evaluate; --replace keeps the rule's current filter unless this is set |
| `--replace` | Update the existing evaluator rule matched by --name on this target |

`--replace` updates the existing rule with the same `--name` on that target and asks for confirmation unless `--yes` is passed.

### `langsmith evaluators upload`

Upload an evaluator function to LangSmith

Usage: `langsmith evaluators upload EVALUATOR_FILE [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--name string` | Evaluator name (required); --replace matches an existing rule on the target by rule or evaluator name |
| `--function string` | Name of the function to upload (required) |
| `--project string` | Target project name (online evaluator) |
| `--dataset string` | Target dataset name (offline evaluator) |
| `--sampling-rate float64` | Fraction of runs to evaluate (0.0-1.0); --replace keeps the rule's current rate unless this is set |
| `--replace` | Update the existing evaluator rule matched by --name on this target |

```bash
langsmith evaluators upload evaluators.py --function exact_match --name exact-match --dataset my-dataset
```

### `langsmith evaluators rule list`

List evaluator rules, optionally for one project, dataset, or evaluator

Usage: `langsmith evaluators rule list [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--project string` | Project name [env: LANGSMITH_PROJECT] |
| `--dataset string` | Only rules on this dataset (name or ID) |
| `--evaluator-id string` | Only rules that use this evaluator |
| `--all` | Include webhook, add-to-dataset, and annotation-queue rules |

```bash
langsmith evaluators rule list --project my-app --format json
```

## Feedback

Feedback is a score, value or comment attached to a run, by a person or an evaluator. Read it alongside runs with `--include-feedback`, and filter on it with `--filter`.

### `langsmith runs list`

List runs matching filter criteria (default: 50, newest first)

Usage: `langsmith runs list [flags]`

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--include-feedback` | Add feedback_stats field |
| `--filter string` | LangSmith filter DSL, e.g. 'and(eq(run_type, "llm"), gte(latency, 5))'. Match metadata with 'and(eq(metadata_key, "user_id"), eq(metadata_value, "u1"))', and inputs or outputs with input_key/input_value or output_key/output_value; metadata.x and inputs.x paths are not supported |
| `--feedback-since string` | Only match feedback modified at or after this timestamp, e.g. 2024-01-15T00:00:00Z (requires a feedback condition in --filter) |

```bash
langsmith runs list --project my-app --filter 'and(eq(feedback_key, "correctness"), eq(feedback_score, 0))' --include-feedback --format json
```

### `langsmith feedback retrieve`

Get a specific feedback.

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--feedback-id string` | — |

```bash
langsmith feedback retrieve --feedback-id 0190a3c4-1234-7abc-8def-0123456789ab --format json
```

### `langsmith feedback update`

Replace an existing feedback entry with a new, modified entry.

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--feedback-id string` | — |
| `--score` | — |
| `--value` | — |
| `--comment string` | — |
| `--correction` | — |

## Annotation queues

Annotation queues hold runs and threads for people to review. Find the queues a run is in, read a queue's items, or add items from an experiment.

### `langsmith annotation-queues retrieve-queues`

Get Annotation Queues For Run

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--run-id string` | ID of the run. |

```bash
langsmith annotation-queues retrieve-queues --run-id 0190a3c4-1234-7abc-8def-0123456789ab --format json
```

### `langsmith annotation-queues retrieve`

Get Annotation Queue

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--queue-id string` | ID of the annotation queue. |

### `langsmith annotation-queues items list`

List RUN and THREAD items in a single annotation queue for one review status section, with opaque cursor pagination.

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--queue-id string` | — |
| `--status string` | Review section: needs_my_review, needs_others_review, or archived |
| `--item-type string` | Filter to RUN or THREAD |
| `--page-size int` | Page size (max 100) |
| `--cursor string` | Opaque pagination cursor |

```bash
langsmith annotation-queues items list --queue-id 0190a3c4-1234-7abc-8def-0123456789ab --status needs_my_review --format json
```

### `langsmith annotation-queues items create`

Add RUN or THREAD items to a single annotation queue.

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--queue-id string` | — |
| `--item any` | — |

### `langsmith annotation-queues populate`

Populate annotation queue with runs from an experiment.

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--queue-id string` | ID of the annotation queue to add runs to. |
| `--session-id string` | Experiments whose runs are added to the queue. Each must be an experiment on a dataset. |

## All commands

Every command in this version of the CLI. Run `langsmith <command> --help` for its flags. Commands marked *confirms* ask before deleting; see [Safety](#safety).

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `langsmith agents create` | Creates an Agent with a caller-assigned ID. |
| `langsmith agents delete` | Permanently deletes an Agent, along with its environments, runtime bindings, runtimes, and tracing projects. *(confirms)* |
| `langsmith agents list` | Returns Agents visible to the caller. |
| `langsmith agents retrieve` | Returns an Agent with the environments visible to the caller. |
| `langsmith agents update` | Updates an Agent's name, source_type, agent_type, or owner_id. |
| `langsmith annotation-queues delete` | Delete Annotation Queue *(confirms)* |
| `langsmith annotation-queues items create` | Add RUN or THREAD items to a single annotation queue. |
| `langsmith annotation-queues items create-status` | Log the caller's reviewer status for a RUN or THREAD annotation queue item. |
| `langsmith annotation-queues items delete-all` | Remove RUN or THREAD items from a single annotation queue by item ID. *(confirms)* |
| `langsmith annotation-queues items list` | List RUN and THREAD items in a single annotation queue for one review status section, with opaque cursor pagination. |
| `langsmith annotation-queues items retrieve-count` | Returns the number of annotation queue items in one status bucket. |
| `langsmith annotation-queues items retrieve-placement` | Resolve a RUN or THREAD item to its current review section and zero-based position for deep linking. |
| `langsmith annotation-queues items update` | Partially update mutable timestamps (added_at, last_reviewed_time) for a RUN or THREAD annotation queue item. |
| `langsmith annotation-queues populate` | Populate annotation queue with runs from an experiment. |
| `langsmith annotation-queues retrieve` | Get Annotation Queue |
| `langsmith annotation-queues retrieve-queues` | Get Annotation Queues For Run |
| `langsmith annotation-queues update` | Update Annotation Queue |
| `langsmith api` | Browse API endpoints and make authenticated requests |
| `langsmith api info` | Show details for a specific API endpoint |
| `langsmith api ls` | List available API endpoints from the OpenAPI spec |
| `langsmith apps delete` | Delete a custom app by ID or name *(confirms)* |
| `langsmith apps dev` | Run the current directory's custom app locally in a real sandbox |
| `langsmith apps init` | Scaffold a starter custom app in a new directory named after the app |
| `langsmith apps list` | List custom apps |
| `langsmith apps pull` | Download a custom app's source into a new directory |
| `langsmith apps push` | Upload the current directory as a custom app |
| `langsmith auth info` | Show the current authentication state |
| `langsmith auth login` | Authenticate with LangSmith using OAuth |
| `langsmith auth signup` | Create a LangSmith account and log the CLI in to it |
| `langsmith auth token` | Print the OAuth access token |
| `langsmith charts preview` | Compute a chart's bucketed data without creating the chart |
